text.p: French holding company Cerus said on Wednesday it would make a special payment to shareholders of 110 francs per share.
Cerus is making the special payment as a recognition that it has not paid dividends for several years since it fell into difficulties at the end of the 1980s, a spokesman for the company said.
The payment marks the company's recovery last year due to the sale of its 28 percent stake in car parts maker Valeo .
When the Valeo sale was announced on November 5, Cerus said it would make an exceptional payment which was expected to be about 100 francs.

Cerus will have 1.8 billion francs in equity capital after the special payment, of which half will be held in liquid assets and the rest in assets designed to generate future liquidity, the company said in a statement.

A shareholders meeting in March will approve the 1996 accounts which will include the automatic increase in capital due to the Valeo disposal and the subsequent reduction in nominal capital due to the 110 franc per share payout, it said.
Holders of a convertible bond which is being repaid early will receive the special payment if they opt to convert their bonds into shares, it said.

Cerus reaffirmed its objective to play its role as an investor-operator, which it said consisted of "taking stakes in activities in industry and services in order to play an active role in adding value to the funds made available by shareholders."
Of the 764 million francs in provisions made for the 1996 year, 650 million was for risks and charges, it said.
The provisions reflected the mark-to-market value of assets and increased the transparency of the company's accounts, the spokesman said.
The provisioning showed the company's desire "to realise these assets and to take advantage of investment opportunities currently available," the company statement said.
